To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) neuritogenesis is regulated by labile disintegrins, (b) disintegrins regulate neurite outgrowth by complexing with cell surface integrin receptors and/or with ganglioside, and (c ) disintegrins can regulate neurite formation in the absence of integrin receptor activation.
neurite formation by F11 subcloned neurons can be regulated by cell surface integrins, GM1, and disintegrins.
neuritogenesis in F11 neuronal hybrid clones is modulated by disintegrins, which are proteins that regulate integrin function and ganglioside function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which cell surface receptors mediate neuritogenesis, and how these mechanisms are regulated.

elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of neuronal differentiation and neuritogenesis, with particular emphasis on cell surface receptor interactions with extracellular matrix proteins and gangliosides.
the mechanisms of neuronal growth control by matrix receptors and their associated regulatory proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the labile proteins (disintegrin(s)) modulate neuritogenesis by regulating the activity of integrin receptors, and that ganglioside-GM1 can modulate the activity of these disintegrins, and thereby regulate neurite outgrowth.
neurite outgrowth in F11 neuronal hybrid clones is modulated by gangioside GM1 and by labile regulatory proteins, referred to as disintegrin, in a complex and dynamic manner.

disintegrins are a class of labile regulatory proteins that are required for normal neuritogenesis on pFN, CTB, and PF4 substrata, but their function is modulated in the absence of protein synthesis and by the presence of GM1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

neurite outgrowth in F11 subclonal neuronal hybrid cells is regulated by at least four mechanisms, mediated by integrins, gangliosides GM1, heparan sulfate, and a labile protein (disintegrin), which can be activated or inactivated by several different experimental manipulations.
neurite outgrowth in F11 neuronal hybrid clones is mediated by three distinct receptor mechanisms, and each of these can be modulated by labile regulatory proteins and ganglioside complexation.
neuritogenesis in the hybrid cells is mediated by a hierarchy of cell surface receptors, with integrins being the most potent and ganglioside-GM1 being the weakest.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the disintegrin paradigm is applicable to the modulation of neuritogenesis in the nervous system, and the disintegrin concept may be useful for understanding the molecular mechanisms of neuritogenesis and neuronal plasticity in general.
